To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the driving force of the formation of diastereomeric associates is the effort of the chiral system to form the most symmetric associate and that (2) the structure of chirally pure compounds contains the information about the outcome of the resolution.

the behaviour of enantio- and diastereomeric mixtures is governed by the same principles; the driving force of the separation of enantiomers and diastereoisomeric mixtures are the same; the separation of diastereomere mixtures can be predicted on the basis of enantiomere separation.
the driving force of diastereoselective reactions is the pursuit of symmetry, which can be realized by the separation of the most symmetric associates (complexes) from the less symmetric associates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the behaviour of chiral compounds in different environments.
the following questions: (1) How does the structure of a chiral compound affect the outcome of the optical resolution?
the prediction of diastereomer separations based on the behaviour of enatiomeric mixtures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the driving force of chiral recognition and separation is the effort of the chiral system to achieve the most symmetric situation.

the driving force of the resolution process is the effort of the diastereoisomeric system to achieve a more symmetric structure, i.e. a system in which the most symmetric associates (the most stable) predominate over the less symmetric ones, the most symmetric associates being those which contain the smallest number of chiral centres.
the structure of the compounds is responsible for the outcome of the resolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a new way to predict the efficiency of diasteroisomer separation.
we can predict, on the basis of molecular structure, the outcome of the resolution.
the behaviour of chiral compounds in solution can be understood on the basis of symmetry considerations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to predict the result of the resolution of racemates on the basis of their behaviour in the distribution of enatiomeric mixtures.
the structure of the resolving agent is not as important as the structure of the compound to be resolved.
it is possible to predict the outcome of diastereoselective reactions and, in particular, the outcome of the resolution of racemates.
